title: specsrbench: benchmarking deep learning against classical deconvolution for galaxy spectral super-resolution
description:
Seven classical deconvolution methods — cubic interpolation, Wiener, Tikhonov, Wiener + total variation, Richardson–Lucy, wavelet-sparse FISTA, and a redshift-informed matched filter — benchmarked against the SR2 deep-learning pipeline of Haghjoo et al. (2026) on 572 held-out JWST/NIRSpec prism spectra from JADES.

The package is code only: model weights are fetched from the Hugging Face Hub, and every derived array is rebuilt from the raw JADES DR4 products by specsrbench build all.

Its headline result is that at the pixel level no method beats cubic interpolation. The deep-learning model leads the raw mean-absolute-error table by 30%, but does so at 0.54 of the reference's amplitude; on a scale-free metric all nine methods fall within 1.2% of each other and it ranks eighth of nine. What survives is that it exceeds the reference's own line signal-to-noise on all four diagnostic lines while recovering 36–53% of true line amplitudes, at false-detection rates up to 0.44 against 0.09 or below for any classical method.

The package also documents four independent ways that tuning a restoration method against a noisy reference by mean absolute error produces a method that scores well and reconstructs badly — smoothing, shrinkage, blurring and merging — together with a guard for each. That material is not specific to spectra.
